title: Ragnar: Exploring Volatile-Channel Vulnerabilities on RDMA NIC
problem: RDMA NICs in data centers face underexplored hardware contention-based side-channel vulnerabilities that enable covert communication and sensitive data extraction.
motivation: RDMA is critical for low-latency data center communication but lacks comprehensive security analysis against hardware-contention attacks.
method: RAGNAR reverse-engineers RDMA network cards by running small test programs to explore their behavior at multiple levels of detail. It identifies vulnerabilities that arise when different programs compete for the same hardware resources, then creates attacks exploiting this competition. The attacks show two capabilities: building hidden communication channels between programs and stealing sensitive data by observing how resource competition affects timing. It demonstrates these attacks work against real distributed database systems.
key_novelty: This is the first comprehensive demonstration of volatile-channel attacks (exploiting hardware contention on network cards) that work against real distributed database systems.
contributions: Comprehensive RDMA NIC reverse engineering at multiple granularities
3.2x bandwidth improvement over state-of-the-art RDMA covert channels (CX-5)
95.6% accuracy in fingerprinting operations on distributed databases

metrics.other: 3.2x bandwidth vs SOTA RDMA attacks, 95.6% fingerprint accuracy
